summary: Two Special Police Officers (SPOs) involved in counter-terror operations were found dead with bullet wounds in the forested reaches of the Chenab Valley in Jammu and Kashmir, highlighting ongoing security challenges in the region's higher altitudes.

background.text: Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Jammu and Kashmir are auxiliary police personnel recruited locally to aid counter-insurgency and anti-terror operations through human intelligence and local terrain familiarity.

Terrorist activity in the Jammu region, including the Pir Panjal and Chenab Valley areas, has witnessed an uptick in recent years, prompting security forces to set up temporary operating bases in dense upper reaches.

prelims_pointer.text: The Chenab Valley region in Jammu and Kashmir encompasses districts like Doda, Kishtwar, and Ramban, featuring rugged terrain and dense forests.

mains_question: Analyze the emerging trends in terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir, with particular focus on the shifting of militant activity towards the forested, higher reaches of the Jammu division. Discuss the strategic measures needed to counter this challenge.

mains_points.text: Security forces have established temporary operating bases in the upper reaches of the Union Territory due to increased terrorist movements in dense forested terrains since 2020.
Local auxiliary forces like Special Police Officers (SPOs) remain critical frontline assets in gathering ground-level intelligence and navigating treacherous forested topography.
Recent incidents indicate persistent asymmetric threats targeting both state police forces and Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) across Jammu and Kashmir.
Strengthening border infiltration grids, enhancing technical surveillance in dense forest cover, and deepening community engagement are essential to eliminate revived terror networks.
